title: Decontam index lacks JevBench/typed-decisions; no 13-gram or option-set test
detail: The only decontamination code in the repo indexes evals/**/*.jsonl utterances plus HobbyLM frozen TSVs, and matches with char-5/bigram/8-gram Jaccard. It never loads JevBench public (231) or the typed-decisions test, never looks at states/criteria/descriptions, and has no option-set check. If the decisions run reuses it (the obvious path, multi-task with route data), the reported contamination count is 0 by construction for the two benchmarks we publish.
evidence: decontam.py:49-63 eval_utterances() globs REPO/evals/**/*.jsonl and HOBBY=/data/evals/hobbylm/data/frozen only; Feats (37-46) holds text-only features; match() 78-90 has no 13-gram path. My own mandated index (jevbench@609a664 + td@80cb93a + route_v1 + live_t1 + external) = {external:570, td/test:400, route_v1:140, jev/hard:111, jev/original:72, jev/easy:48, live_t1:43}; decontam.py covers only the last 3.
fix: New decontam for decisions: load jevbench datasets/public/{easy,original,hard}.jsonl@609a664 and td all/test parquet@80cb93a; per item concatenate state_text(state)+instructions+criteria/descriptions; drop on ANY shared word 13-gram (containment, not Jaccard) plus option-set rule (see decisions-2); write counts per source to the run report.

title: Identical-option-set rule is degenerate on benchmark option sets
detail: typed-decisions reuses a handful of generic option sets across 2000 decisions and 200 noul have no criteria at all (default true/false); score options are '0'..'n-1'. A key-only comparison flags every synthetic noul/score item (so it will be quietly loosened or skipped); a text comparison of route items flags all route datums because route_v1 uses the same 41-option catalog. Either way the 'counts must be 0' report is meaningless unless the rule is pinned down.
evidence: Independent count: td test 2000 decisions -> 16 distinct normalized option-set signatures (600 choice/600 noul/800 score); td noul 400 with criteria, 200 without; JevBench 109 distinct sets, all 74 noul use criteria {false,true}; 0 signature overlap between JevBench and td.
fix: Define: choice -> drop if (sorted option keys, normalized descriptions) equals a benchmark set; noul -> compare criteria texts only when present; score -> compare level description texts; exempt route datums vs route_v1 option catalog explicitly (utterance checks still apply) and report exempt counts separately.

title: Route regression would be measured with the wrong renderer and n=140
detail: Brief runs route_v1 through the new Tinker-sampler Decider for bench/systemone, i.e. GenericRenderer (_decision: stock system prompt, 'State/Question' user text, choices in user turn). Route datums are trained and served with RouteDecisionRenderer (route system prompt with choices in system, 'Context: app=... | ...' user line). Measuring the multi-task adapter on a prompt it was never trained on for routing gives a spurious drop (or hides a real one). Also 1 point on 140 items = 1.4 items; SE at top-1 0.918 is sqrt(.918*.082/140)=2.3 pts, so a 1-point gate is noise.
evidence: Tokenizer check (Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, transformers 5.5.4): GenericRenderer static prefix = 42 tokens decoding to 'Answer the user's question by picking exactly one of the choices they supply...'; training route_render.py:29-35,106-131 renders ROUTE_SYSTEM with choices + ROUTE_USER. eval_route.py:27-60 already evaluates route_v1/val via render_route.
fix: Score route regression with training/src/muselet_train/eval_route.py (--set route_v1 and --set val) for both the route-only and the multi-task checkpoint; report paired per-item deltas (McNemar) on val, not only route_v1.

title: noul option order flips with criteria presence: position-shortcut risk
detail: With criteria {false,true} the order follows criteria keys (JevBench: false=choice#A); without criteria it is [true='Yes', false='No'] (true=choice#A). td test has 200/600 noul without criteria. Synthetic data generated 'with criteria' only (brief line 45) never trains the default form, and if gold is skewed by form the model learns 'A' instead of the question. Also a Tinker Decider re-implementing this order would silently break parity.
evidence: generic_decide.py:27-30 quoted; JevBench public noul 74/74 have criteria (false first); td noul 400 crit / 200 no-crit.
fix: Generate >=1/3 noul without criteria; balance gold over choice#A/B within each form; report gold-position histogram per type and option count; have the Tinker Decider import _decision/_choices rather than copy them.

title: Before/after benchmark numbers would mix MLX-4bit and Tinker-bf16
detail: Baseline row is MLX base Qwen3.5-4B-4bit vs DeskMind 8-bit; the planned 'after' numbers come from the Tinker sampler (bf16 base + LoRA). A before/after delta across precision/runtime is not attributable to training, and 4-bit vs 8-bit is not tuned-vs-tuned (standing decision). Publishing it as 'Muselet vs DeskMind' would be a wrong-result-presented-as-correct risk.

title: No token parity reference exists for the generic decision path
detail: The only parity reference is route-only; the cloud/bench test only asserts static prefix, choice_pos and single-token labels, never equality with a training renderer. title: A 20k-decision multi-task run likely exceeds the $25 gate
detail: Each typed question is a separate datum that repeats the full state, so cost scales with state length; hard-split-like states are ~8x td states. Plan the estimate before generating 25k items.
evidence: Measured rendered tokens/question: JevBench easy 158, original 164, hard 1265 (max 3987); td 250; route datum 931 (parity_300). Rate from phase1_main: $29.45/37.59M = $0.78/M. 20k decisions at 1/3 hard-length (avg ~590) = 11.8M + 30% route replay 8.6k x 931 = 8.0M -> 19.8M/epoch = $15.5; 2 epochs = $31 > $25. Headroom: $150-37-32 = $81.
fix: Cap hard-length states at ~1/4 of items or 1 epoch, or batch several questions per state into one datum only if inference renders the same; post estimate and get lead OK before launch.

title: Code-gold options leak the answer via descriptions, padding and verbatim values
detail: Gold is recoverable without the reasoning the family is meant to teach: distractor descriptions say they are wrong ('A conversion one pound too high', 'overcharges', padding 'alternate_NN ... does not satisfy the stated conditions'), the state states the tiered fee outright ('that fee is $X'), the cap question quotes the computed total, and the weight noul is always true. The student learns description/wording cues, not computation. Lead amendment 2 does not cover these.
evidence: Simulated 300 records/family@c08a96d (seed 2): filtering options whose description matches /too (high|low)|overcharg|undercharg|does not satisfy/ leaves exactly the gold on numeric 193/300 and temporal 79/300 choice questions (100% correct); picking the unique non-padding key that appears verbatim in state+instructions is right on long_policy 261/300 and numeric 97/97; 80-91% of choice questions are padded with self-declared wrong alternate_NN options (real options per question: 2.0-3.0).

title: MLX backend silently ignores calibration temperatures
detail: --temperature-probs/--temperature-conf are only passed to TinkerDecider. The MLX path (the Mac ship/bench path after 4-bit export) constructs GenericMLXDecider(args.model_path) with no temperature and returns a plain softmax, and it has no separate confidence distribution. Any 'calibrated' Tinker numbers (HANDOFF step 1, -cal run) will not be what the Mac serves or benches, so calibrated KL/ECE claims will not reproduce on the shipped model.
evidence: cli.py:34-36@f6fb133: `if args.backend == "mlx": decider = GenericMLXDecider(args.model_path)`; temperatures only at :41-42 (tinker). generic_decide.py:130 `def __init__(self, model_path: str)`; :226 `probabilities = self.mx.softmax(logits[self.mx.array(token_ids)], axis=0)` (no /T).
fix: Add temperature_probs/temperature_conf to GenericMLXDecider.__init__ and divide logits before softmax (mirror tinker_backend), pass them from cli.py for --backend mlx, and have the server load calibration.json next to the adapter.

title: near_miss_values centers distractors on gold: 'pick the middle' shortcut
detail: Distractors are added at answer±radius*step for growing radius, so the gold is symmetrically surrounded and tends to be the medoid of the numeric option set. A model can score on code-gold choice questions by picking the central value without computing; this does not transfer to JevBench/TD and is consistent with the hard-tier drop (.658 -> .622) as code-gold share grew.

title: inline() decider lacks temperatures after cloud/decisions merge: AttributeError
detail: planner-verify adds GenericMLXDecider.inline(), which builds the object via cls.__new__ and sets only mx/model/body/lm_head/renderer/caches. cloud/decisions@08dae49 (3292c44) makes _score_renderings read self.temperature_probs and self.temperature_conf, which only __init__ sets. The two branches merge without conflicts, and the result raises AttributeError on the first Planner.decide() call. That breaks the planner's System One verify step: planner.py:280-285 calls inline() and the error goes out through the worker future (planner.py:170-171). Neither branch's tests catch it, because each one is green on its own and MLX can't run on Linux CI.
evidence: Scratch merge of origin/cloud/decisions + origin/cloud/planner-verify: 'Automatic merge went well'. Merged generic_decide.py: inline() at 178-190 has no temperature_* assignment, and lines 277/280 use self.temperature_probs / self.temperature_conf; these attributes are set only at 164-165 in __init__. planner.py:284@d22b9a9: self._decider = GenericMLXDecider.inline(self.model, self.model_path). Static only; MLX not runnable here.
fix: In inline(): add temperature_probs=1.0, temperature_conf=1.0 kwargs, validate them as __init__ does, and set self.temperature_probs/self.temperature_conf. Alternatively, give the class defaults: `temperature_probs = 1.0; temperature_conf = 1.0`. Add a test that builds the decider via __new__ the way inline() does and calls _score_renderings with a stub model.

title: Live on main: planner done-verifier always errors (no temperatures in inline)
evidence: PR #39 merged as ba9f29a. On main@e9fb42d, generic_decide.py:276 reads self.temperature_probs, which only __init__ sets (163). inline() at 177-190 builds the decider via cls.__new__ and never sets it. planner.py:386 calls inline(), and --verify-done defaults to on (cli.py:336, serve_brain.sh:50). So every planner 'done' raises AttributeError, which is caught at orchestrator.py:1661-1673 as 'verifier unavailable'. The fallback at 2696-2699 accepts done only when n_executed == 0, so the model verifier never runs and chained tasks get extra planner rounds at about 2.6 s p50 each (think 512). The design rule that DONE is verified is silently off. Static analysis only (MLX can't run on Linux); the Mac repro is any 2-step planner task with VERIFY_DONE=on, where the trace shows planner.verify error="'GenericMLXDecider' object has no attribute 'temperature_probs'".
fix: In inline(), add `self.temperature_probs = 1.0; self.temperature_conf = 1.0`, or define both as class attributes defaulting to 1.0. Add a Linux test that builds the decider via __new__ the way inline() does, with a stub model, and calls _score_renderings.

title: Router tau reused, unmeasured, as the gate for superseding a pending slot or a CONFIRM prompt
detail: _new_command() treats a router hit (res.p_top >= self.tau and top not in ASK/ANSWER, orchestrator.py:637@dba9094) as a new command. server.py:61-71 uses it during an open CONFIRM: a recognized utterance runs as a new task and the confirm is superseded. self.tau (.50 for it3, .35 for it2) was fitted for route top-1 accuracy, not for a binary 'is this a new command or an answer to the pending question' decision. No eval measures the false-supersede rate on replies to pending prompts (for example 'go ahead', 'send the email', 'yes, play it'). The only guards are regexes: _CMD_VERB, _DEICTIC 'it|them' and a yes/ok list. Superseding a confirm fails safe (nothing is sent), but it drops the user's pending task. AGENTS.md: 'Confidence thresholds are fitted on eval failures.'
evidence: orchestrator.py:637@dba9094 `if res.p_top >= self.tau and res.top not in ("ASK", "ANSWER"): return f"router:{res.top}"`; server.py:61-71@dba9094 confirm_interrupt -> _run_utterance; test_pending_new_command.py uses FakeEngine with hand-set p_top (lines 124-130), so it does not measure real router behaviour on replies. 'go ahead' passes _CMD_VERB ('go') and none of the guards (not deictic, not in the yes list), so only the router decides it. Not run here: needs the Mac router.
fix: Before enabling: build a small eval of replies vs new commands made while a pending slot or confirm is open (both from live traces), report the false-supersede rate at the serving tau, and fit a separate supersede threshold on it (or require top != the pending skill). Add 'go ahead'/'do that' to the continue/yes guards.

title: open_ended_redirect overrides correct router decisions: 3.9% of route_v1_clean and 6.7% of route_v2 gold skill routes go to the planner
detail: With OPEN_ENDED on by default (serve_brain.sh:55@fd87f69), a confident safe router label (including ANSWER) is replaced by a planner run whenever a keyword app hint matches and the label is not in hint.skills. Even with a perfect router (gold label fed in), this sends 4/103 route_v1_clean cases (open_app 'fire up safari', open_app 'pull up system settings', open_url 'youtube dot com', start_timer 'remind me ... with a timer') and 64/955 route_v2 cases (mostly open_app/hide_app/set_volume naming an app) to the planner. That costs one-pass skill speed and lowers the measured route accuracy. None of this is in the open-ended report, which only measures the 25 open-ended cases.
evidence: reviews/decisions/repro/oe_redirect_flips.py on review/decisions (pure-Python, gold labels, catalog risk from skills/catalog.json@fd87f69): route_v1_clean 103 -> 4 flipped; route_v2 955 -> 64 flipped. Orchestrator path: orchestrator.py:1131-1138@fd87f69 `redirect = open_ended_redirect(label, text, self.catalog.risk(label)); if redirect is not None: return await self._planner_loop(text, trace)`.
fix: Gate the redirect on low router confidence (p_top < tau, or MULTI_STEP), or skip it when the label is a launch or system skill (open_app, open_url, hide_app, set_volume, start_timer). Re-run the repro plus an end-to-end route_v1_clean/route_v2 eval with OPEN_ENDED on before making it the default, and require 0 gold flips on route_v1_clean.

title: Finish-evidence done gate accepts done from the planner's own URL and a mis-extracted subject, bypassing expect and model verification
detail: For search goals, evidence() is True when every subject word appears in the window title OR the URL; with no obs url it falls back to self._last_ok_url, i.e. the URL the planner itself just opened (set whenever open_url/url returned ok). The query string contains the subject by construction, so the check is self-fulfilling: a still-loading or 404 page passes. When it passes, done is accepted with method=finish, p_yes=None, before the last_exp_ok / model-verify branches. This contradicts AGENTS.md 'DONE is verified by the harness, never trusted' for exactly the loading case the lane brief targets. Separately, _subject cuts at the first on/in/for/..., so 'search youtube for jazz' yields subject 'youtube' (any YouTube page passes).
evidence: Repro (pure Python, finish.py@9b2e512): criterion('search youtube for jazz') -> ('search','youtube',...); evidence('search','youtube',obs={'window':'Zen Browser','text':''},url='https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=jazz') -> True. criterion('find flights to boston on google') -> subject 'flights'; evidence(..., obs={'window':'404 Not Found'}, url='https://www.google.com/search?q=flights+boston') -> True.
fix: Use only post-action observed state (obs title, obs url from the browser) as evidence, never _last_ok_url; require the page not be in the loading state from item 1; strip site names from the subject (or take the phrase after 'for'); add regression tests for the two repros. Measure accept/reject vs the model verifier on recorded traces before merge.
